examples: You were in session api, opened your review layout, then session web. Cmd+[ takes you back to the review layout, Cmd+[ again to api, and Cmd+] forward to the layout.
With three layout tabs open in the layout bar, Cmd+2 opens the second and Cmd+9 the last, from anywhere in the app.
how_to: Cmd+[ goes back to the session or layout you were on before; Cmd+] goes forward again. Like a browser: a fresh jump drops the forward list, and closed sessions and deleted layouts are skipped.
Each window keeps its own history, in memory, at most 50 places. Only what you opened counts.
Cmd+1 to Cmd+8 open layout tab 1 to 8 in the layout bar, in its saved order; Cmd+9 opens the last tab. No tab N: nothing happens.
A text box keeps its keys: these chords do nothing while you type in one. A browser pane keeps its own keys too. The keys are listed on the keyboard shortcuts page.
Mac only. In Safari, and for Cmd+digits in some Chrome builds, the browser may take the key first; the desktop app always gets it.
In the Mac app the Go menu has Back and Forward (Cmd+[ and Cmd+]) and the last 10 sessions and layouts this window was on; pick one to jump there.
media_exempt: keyboard only: a still image cannot show a chord moving between sessions
name: Session history and layout tab keys
summary: Cmd+[ and Cmd+] step back and forward through the sessions and layouts you opened, and Cmd+1 to 9 open layout tab N.
where: Anywhere in the app on a Mac, terminal focused or not.
The Go menu in the Mac app's menu bar.
